1. Install the package mlbench and use the follows to import the data

```{r}
library(caret)
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("PimaIndiansDiabetes.csv")
head(df)
```

```{r}
# Cleaning
df <- df |> rename(target = diabetes)

df$target <- as.factor(unlist(df$target))

colSums(is.na(df))
```

```{r}
# Split Data into Training and Testing
set.seed(42)

splitIndex <- createDataPartition(df$target, p = 0.70, list = FALSE)

df_train <- df[ splitIndex,]
df_test <- df[-splitIndex,]
```


Train and Test a decision tree and a random forest with caret. Plot the variable importance of these models. 

```{r}
# Decision Tree
dt <- train(target~., data = df_train, method = "rpart2", maxdepth = 3)
pred <- predict(dt, df_test)

cm <- confusionMatrix(data = pred, reference = df_test$target, positive = "pos")

cm$overall[1]
```


```{r}
# Plot DT Importance
plot(varImp(dt))
```


```{r}
# Random Forest
rf <- train(target~., data = df_train, method = "rf", ntree = 1000)
pred <- predict(rf, df_test)


cm <- confusionMatrix(data = pred, reference = df_test$target, positive = "pos")

cm$overall[1]
```


```{r}
# Plot RF Importance
plot(varImp(rf))
```


2. Train and Test a `glmnet` model. Plot the variable importance of the model. 

```{r}
# `glmnet` model
library(glmnet)

glmnet <- train(target~., data = df_train, method = "glmnet")
pred <- predict(glmnet, df_test)

cm = confusionMatrix(data = pred, reference = df_test$target, positive = "pos")

cm$overall[1]
```


```{r}
# Plot Importance
plot(varImp(glmnet))
```


3. Train and test two models that are not `ranger`, `glmnet` or `rpart`  with caret. If possible, plot the variable importance of the model. 

```{r}
# Model 1: `knn`
df_train <- as.data.frame(df_train) # changing data type from tibble to data frame to plot variable importance

# tibble handles column indexing differently than data frames, so when extracting variable importance, it accidentally extracts outcome variable as a 1 column list rather than flat vector

knn <- train(target~., data = df_train, method = "knn")
pred <- predict(knn, df_test)

cm = confusionMatrix(data = pred, reference = df_test$target, positive = "pos")

cm$overall[1]
```


```{r}
# Plot Importance
importance_knn <- varImp(knn)
plot(importance_knn)
```


```{r}
# Model 2: `LogitBoost`

# boosted logistic regression is an additive model that minimizes the negative log-likelihood (log loss)
library(caTools)

logistic <- train(target~., data = df_train, method = "LogitBoost")
pred <- predict(logistic, df_test)

cm = confusionMatrix(data = pred, reference = df_test$target, positive = "pos")

cm$overall[1]
```


```{r}
# Plot Importance
plot(varImp(logistic))
```
